answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a bonded-entry vault: every new agent must lock a deposit of jade tokens for thirty epochs, earning nothing while locked. The lock is time-gated and non-transferable, so a sybil farmer spinning up ten thousand sockpuppets must park ten thousand deposits that sit idle and harden like shale, illiquid and unusable. Honest agents pay only once and reuse their standing; attackers pay the lock cost per identity. After the epochs elapse the vault refunds, so the barrier is pure opportunity cost -- identity creation is priced by the cost of capital, not by rent.
